observation: Gumroad's features page describes the platform as a powerful but simple e-commerce platform that enables selling digital services such as books, memberships, and courses directly to an audience.
Gumroad's features page states a flexible page editor is available for sellers to build a storefront and customize site colors, framed as usable for sellers without an existing website.
Gumroad's features page states that sellers can create simple memberships giving customers access to a library of content for as long as they are subscribed.
Gumroad's features page states that the platform can generate license keys for sellers of software products.
Gumroad's pricing page states a fee of 10% + $0.50 per transaction for all sales through seller profiles or direct links to customers.
Gumroad's pricing page states a 30% per-transaction fee when new customers find and buy from a seller through the Gumroad Discover marketplace.
Gumroad's pricing page states the platform does not charge a monthly fee, and instead deducts fees as a small percentage of every sale.
Gumroad's pricing page states that since January 1, 2025, Gumroad handles all tax obligations for sellers, including worldwide sales tax collection and remittance.

Gumroad's pricing page states that the platform will collect taxes in regions where it has tax obligations as a merchant of record, with the scope varying by location, and that appropriate tax collection for each sale is handled automatically.

Gumroad's pricing page describes the platform as supporting sales of digital products, e-books, courses, tutorials, and memberships, and states that creators across industries including digital artists, writers, musicians, entrepreneurs, and SaaS creators use it, with the qualifier 'almost anything' applied to scope.
Gumroad's pricing page states that how sellers are paid—whether through direct deposit or PayPal—varies by country.

Gumroad's prohibited items policy page (last revised April 17, 2019) states that prohibited products and activities are disallowed almost always because they violate U.S. federal law, are prohibited by card network rules, or are restricted by payment processing partners.

Gumroad's prohibited items policy page (last revised April 17, 2019) lists item #19 as prohibiting currency exchange, virtual currency, cryptocurrency, NFTs, and monetizable digital credits that can be converted to physical or digital goods or exit the virtual world.

Gumroad's prohibited items policy page (last revised April 17, 2019) states that changes to the prohibited items list may occur abruptly and without notice due to unpredictable card network rules, legislation, and payment processor relationships, and that changes take effect immediately.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that the platform enables sellers to appoint Gumroad as their non-exclusive reseller of digital products that Gumroad deems eligible for resale through the services.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that Gumroad holds sole discretion to determine and change eligible product categories for resale at any time, that Gumroad is the merchant of record for all resales, and that sellers are prohibited from issuing invoices or demanding payment directly from buyers.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that the Gumroad Fee is automatically deducted from the buyer's purchase price, with the remainder (less taxes and other charges) paid to the seller as the Supplier Fee on an agreed settlement schedule that is subject to change at Gumroad's discretion.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that Gumroad handles buyer refund, chargeback, and dispute requests at its sole discretion, and that sellers are responsible for reimbursing Gumroad for any amounts paid to buyers in connection with refunds, chargebacks, or disputes.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that regardless of listed currency, all transactions settle in USD, with exchange rates sourced from openexchangerates.org and the rate accuracy not guaranteed.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that Gumroad, as the merchant of record, is responsible for indirect tax administration, collection, reporting, and remittance, except in limited circumstances where the buyer may be responsible as outlined in Section 10.5.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that Gumroad currently uses Stripe, Inc. and its affiliates, and PayPal, as third-party service providers for payment processing including card acceptance and merchant settlement.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that sellers must upload digital product files in a format approved by Gumroad (including but not limited to .mp3, .pdf, .png, .jpeg files), and that Gumroad will promptly facilitate delivery to the buyer upon purchase.

Gumroad's Terms of Service (effective January 1, 2025) states that unless a user opts out within 30 days, disputes must be pursued individually rather than as class actions, the right to jury trial is waived, and disputes are governed by California law consistent with the Federal Arbitration Act.

Gumroad's help center article on Getting Paid states that seller payout method depends on the country in which the seller is physically located; if direct deposit is unavailable in that country, payouts occur via PayPal; and if PayPal is also unavailable in that country, there is currently no way to pay the seller.

Gumroad's help center article on Getting Paid states that PayPal payouts are always processed in USD, usually in 1-3 business days, require an individual or business PayPal account without restrictions, and that Payoneer, Wise, check, money order, and wire transfer are not supported as payout methods.

Gumroad's help center article on Getting Paid states that sale amounts sit in the seller's Gumroad balance for at least 7 days before being paid out, and that it is not possible to customize the payout schedule.

A Gumroad help center article (dated May 12, 2022 per search index) states the platform enables creators in more than 160 countries to accept payments, with payout method determined by country of residence: direct bank deposit or debit card in listed countries, and verified PayPal required for all others.

A Gumroad help center article (dated May 12, 2022 per search index) states that if PayPal is not supported in a seller's country, Gumroad cannot pay them out, and explicitly lists Payoneer, wire deposits, and bitcoin as unavailable alternatives.

A Gumroad help center article on Account Suspension (dated July 23, 2024 per search index) states that when an account is suspended for a high chargeback rate, the balance is held for 30-45 days, after which the remaining balance is paid if given clearance by banking partners.

A Gumroad help center article on payout settings (dated November 27, 2023 per search index) states that Gumroad uses Stripe to process all credit card payments and bank payouts, and that Gumroad is subject to Stripe's policies and regulations.

A Gumroad help center article on file size limits (dated November 20, 2023) states that free products have a 250 MB file size limit, products priced above $0.99 have a 16 GB per-file limit with unlimited file count, and the 'Download all' button is only shown when total content size is less than 500 MB.

A Gumroad help center article on selling digital products (dated July 31, 2023) states it costs $0 to start selling on Gumroad with no monthly fees, and that Gumroad charges a 10% flat fee per sale, excluding credit card processing and PayPal fees.

A Gumroad help center article on refund policy (dated May 10, 2023) states that Gumroad reserves the right to issue refunds within 90 days of purchase at its discretion to prevent chargebacks, even if a seller has a no-refund policy, and that customers can additionally issue chargebacks at any time through their credit card.
A Gumroad help center article on fees states a 10% flat fee for sales made on Gumroad's website, excluding credit card processing and PayPal fees. The snippet appears truncated.
A Gumroad help center article on fees states that for sales made through the Gumroad mobile app, the total fee is 40%, broken down as 10% to Gumroad and 30% to the App Store or Google Play Store.

A Gumroad help center article on customer interaction (dated October 27, 2022) states that customers have a specified amount of time, usually 90 days from the date of sale, to request a chargeback through their bank, and that Gumroad as the merchant cannot prevent chargebacks from happening but will dispute them in some cases.

A Gumroad help center article on Gumroad Discover (dated July 22, 2024) states that to be eligible for the Discover mobile app, products cannot be free and cannot exceed $100 in sales price; all app sales are final with no refunds from Gumroad or sellers; refund requests for in-app purchases must go to Apple or Google; and there is a 40% fee for all in-app sales.
A blog author reported total sales of $3,271 on Gumroad from POD experiments in the first six months, selling art prints, a course, and a merch drop.

A seller in a forum post (page undated) reported using Gumroad to sell sample packs over the last 2 years and described the overall experience as good, but stated dissatisfaction with recent unspecified platform changes and an intent to switch platforms.

A blog post (source date approximately July 2025) by a seller described using Gumroad's abandoned cart recovery email feature, writing a separate email for each product left in the cart for personalization, with the process automated after a one-time setup.
A blog post (dated January 29, 2026) reported that a seller's Gumroad digital products received a total of 7,068 views during 2025 (January through December).

A blog post (dated December 7, 2025) by a seller described building small educational HTML products for Gumroad (vocabulary games, reading comprehension activities, Jeopardy reviews) that the seller uses in their own classroom, with each product taking 15-30 minutes to produce with AI assistance.

A blog post (dated November 2025) states that many Gumroad users faced delayed payouts, poor customer support, and account suspensions without clear reasons, and that some people struggled to get their money back.
A blog post (dated October 25, 2025) by a seller reported paying $16.59 in fees from $110 total sales on Gumroad, with editorial commentary on how fees grow with higher sales volumes.
A blog post (dated September 7, 2025) by a seller stated that traffic metrics (views) on Gumroad do not equate to dollars in sales.
A blog post (dated March 2026) by a seller reported having 35 Gumroad product listings and receiving zero organic traffic (described as 'zero footfall').

A blog post (dated February 6, 2026) reported that a seller received a Gumroad '2025 in review' email stating they earned a total of $61,411 in digital product sales and ranked #238 among all creators.
A blog post (dated November 2, 2025) by a seller reported making approximately $21 in total sales within a week of starting on Gumroad, described as their first few sales.
A blog post (dated March 2026) by a seller announced sharing their actual Gumroad dashboard data covering 50+ digital products including sales and failures.

A blog post (dated November 16, 2025) by a seller described sending multiple emails to Gumroad support over an unresolved account verification issue, following all instructions seen online including verifying, re-verifying, and checking bank details.
A blog post (dated April 2026) by a seller reported earning $65.15 in 4 hours from a PDF product and described stacking $50-$200 in organic daily revenue on Gumroad.

A blog post (dated July 20, 2025) states that Gumroad will not promote a product through the Discover page until the seller earns their first $10, with the author characterizing this as no free exposure from Gumroad before the threshold is met.
A blog post (dated November 12, 2025) by a seller stated that in three years on Gumroad they made a grand total of $139.96.

A blog post (accessed April 2026, content referencing May 1, 2025 sale) by a seller stated they had not yet gained the confidence to sell on Gumroad and described pricing a product and uncertainty about buyer willingness to pay as the primary barrier.
A blog post (dated January 24, 2026) stated that Gumroad's rating system is publicly visible on product pages and that a single 1-star review at the top of a product page degrades buyer trust.

A blog post (dated December 2025) by a seller reported making their first sale within hours of publishing their first product and stated that by end of 2025 the experiment generated nearly $15,000 in sales on Gumroad.

A blog post (dated March 24, 2026) by a seller described temporarily switching to Gumroad to start selling right away when Lemon Squeezy approval was pending, noting ease of setup and clean interface, but perceiving Gumroad fees as high, and subsequently migrating back to Lemon Squeezy once approved.

A seller forum post (dated March 31, 2026) reported having 26 products on Gumroad with zero organic views and zero views from Gumroad Discover, with all views coming from the seller's own traffic, and attributed this to Gumroad Discover only showing products after a seller's first sale.

A Gumroad Discover search results page (accessed April 2026) for the 3D Character Design subcategory displayed 75 products sorted by hot_and_new, with filter options including tags (e.g., ffxiv with 34 products), file types (e.g., zip with 31), and a Show NSFW toggle.

The Gumroad homepage (accessed April 2026) displayed the headline 'Sell anything' with supporting copy citing video lessons and monthly subscriptions as examples of formats the platform was created to support.

The Gumroad homepage (accessed April 2026) displayed a Discover section featuring a list of category tags including blender, meditation, comic, notion template, textures, procreate, 3d model, hypnosis, manga, investing, mockup, brushes, font, art, after effects, education, fitness, vrchat, ableton, yoga, fiction, assets, sheet music, and others.

A Gumroad Discover page (accessed April 2026) displayed a category navigation structure with top-level categories including Drawing & Painting, Design, 3D, Music & Sound Design, Films, Self Improvement, Software Development, and Education, each with multiple subcategories.

The Gumroad Discover page (accessed April 2026) displayed the text 'Browse over 1.6 million free and premium digital products in education, tech, design, and more categories from Gumroad creators and online entrepreneurs.'

A Gumroad Discover search results page (accessed April 2026) displayed additional category navigation covering Education, Business & Money, Photography, Writing & Publishing, Comics & Graphic Novels, Fitness & Health, Fiction Books, Audio, and Recorded Music, each with subcategories.

A Gumroad help center article (dated July 27, 2022) stated that adding a category and tags to products helps Gumroad show them on Discover, and that if a seller has nine or more products, their product tags appear on their Gumroad profile for customer filtering.

A Gumroad help center article (dated July 26, 2024) stated that products can be free or priced up to USD $5,000, and that sellers can enable pay-what-you-want pricing by adding a '+' to a product's minimum price.

A Gumroad help center article (dated November 20, 2023) stated that free products have a file size limit of 250 MB and products priced above $0.99 have a file size limit of 16 GB per file, with an unlimited number of files per product.

A Gumroad help center article (dated February 21, 2022) stated that the most common items sold on Gumroad are e-books, films, music, software, and tutorials, and that memberships and one-time purchase products (both digital and physical) are also available.

A Gumroad help center article (dated July 22, 2024) stated that once unspecified eligibility criteria are satisfied, a product will be listed on Discover if a category has been selected for it in the product edit page share tab.

A Gumroad help center article (dated July 22, 2024) stated that NSFW products must be tagged via toggle and will only be displayed to buyers who opt in to see adult content, and that sellers can improve Discover placement by agreeing to an increased Discover fee charged only on Discover-originated sales.

A Gumroad help center article (dated June 29, 2024) described membership product tiers as seller-configurable versions within a membership that support varying access levels, software license levels (e.g., Individual or Team), and add-on services such as coaching calls or community access.
